privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.description: How this documentation website handles visitor information.
privacy.notice: This notice covers the documentation website only. Products built from the starter need their own policy based on the services and data they use.

sections.heading: Information processed
paragraphs: This website serves public documentation. It does not create customer accounts, accept payments, or store product uploads.
The hosting provider may process routine request data such as an IP address, user agent, requested URL, and timestamp to deliver and protect the site.

sections.heading: Optional analytics and preferences
paragraphs: Analytics is disabled unless a Google Analytics 4 property and this website’s hostname are configured. The Google tag is loaded only after you explicitly allow analytics. We do not track installations or activity in products built from the starter.

Our events contain public page categories, language, fixed interaction labels and, when present, approved campaign labels. We do not send form contents, email addresses, arbitrary page paths, full referrers or raw query strings in these events. Google also receives network information, including your IP address and browser headers, and standard analytics session and device information. Advertising storage, Google signals and advertising personalization are disabled by this integration.

Google Analytics uses visitor and session identifiers in cookies after permission is granted. We configure this site’s analytics cookies with a sushi prefix, this hostname only and a 30-day lifetime without refreshing the expiry on each visit. This site also stores your accepted or declined choice under sushi:analytics-consent:ga4:v1 in local storage. If storage is unavailable, the choice lasts only for the current page session.

Analytics settings in the footer, or the floating control on documentation pages, let you withdraw permission. This stops future events from the integration and removes accessible analytics cookies created by it; it does not retract information already sent to Google. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control override earlier permission. The site may also store necessary preferences such as language or theme.

sections.heading: External links
paragraphs: Documentation links to GitHub and third-party provider documentation. Their privacy practices apply after you follow those links.

sections.heading: Questions
paragraphs: Open an issue in the linked source repository for questions about this notice or the documentation website.

proof.title: The details matter after launch.
proof.description: Follow the source and tests behind the claims. These are the systems that keep working when a request repeats or a job is interrupted.

items.title: Billing with a paper trail
items.body: Idempotent payment handling, append-only credits, and replay-safe refunds keep financial effects traceable.

items.title: Work that can recover
items.body: Durable jobs, bounded retries, and cancellation checks preserve progress beyond a browser request.

items.title: Clear ownership boundaries
items.body: Workspace-scoped authorization and private file access keep customer resources in their own context.

items.question: Can I use this for a commercial product?
items.answer: Yes. The starter is open source under the MIT License. You can adapt it for commercial products; keep the required license notice. Hosting and third-party services are separate.

items.question: Do I need every application?
items.answer: No. Core runs the customer app and worker. Operations adds admin, and Publishing adds Content Studio. Profiles choose local tools and build targets; they do not change plan entitlements.

items.question: Does it include a working AI provider?
items.answer: The local image and video examples use mock providers and stay disabled in production. Add your provider, product rules, and validation while keeping the billing, storage, and recovery contracts.

items.question: What do I still need before launch?
items.answer: Your product workflow, identity, pricing, provider accounts, reviewed legal policies, and deployment configuration. The launch and upgrade guides explain the checks and operational responsibilities.
